answers.explanation: Shola's father shrewdly measures the stranger's capacity to pay and uses a manoeuvre to raise his fee, so he is greedy.
The passage does not say the father could row the stranger alone, and he claims his boatman is needed, so that statement is not true.
The passage describes the stranger as handsome, arrogant and deep-voiced, and his voice disturbs Shola.
Shola's father's manoeuvre is a strategy to raise his fee.
The stranger speaks gloomily and is disappointed, so he is in a bad mood.
The writer cites the 1936 Olympic Games as an example of sporting contests leading to orgies of hatred.
The writer says that on the village green it is possible to play simply for the fun of it and exercise.
The passage says a fight between white and coloured boxers before a mixed audience is a horrible sight, so boxing generates ill-will among spectators of different races.
The passage says that running, jumping and kicking a ball are seriously believed to be tests of national virtue.
Mimic warfare is a warfare imitated in sport, so mimic means imitated.
The snake is described as moving slowly and cautiously, which is why it is referred to as something strange.
The writer's antipathy towards the snake melts away and he shares its perplexity, so the feeling changes from antipathy to perplexity.
Once the snake lunged, its coiled body could not support itself on the ledge, so no recovery was possible.
The passage says the snake fell because its own coiled body overbalanced, so the plant was not entirely to blame.
The wind gusts drive the plant's twigs against the snake's head, so the wind prompted the encounter.
The nightmare refers to all the hazards of famine, disease and disaster that made life hideous.
Man had no answer or satisfactory solution to natural disasters, so they were regarded as a curse.
The phrase means starvation still afflicts man.
The passage says the working population engaged in agriculture is too small to produce enough food.
The passage says many religious sects object to many of the birth control measures.
The passage is about preparations by aggressive forces that would carry nuclear disaster into Third World territories.
Aggressive in this context means militant.
The central point is that aggressive forces are ready to carry the nuclear battle into the developing nations.
The author says current developments indicate that nuclear disaster would spread into developing countries.
The passage says a nuclear exchange in the Northern Hemisphere would have a global aftermath making mankind's continued existence impossible.
